summary: A trainer on a new hire's first days asks about things they might not know yet in a way that makes not knowing fine.
realLife: Recorded orientation lectures show trainers asking knowledge-probing questions about what newcomers may have learned before the job, worded so no one is assumed to already know the answer.
sources: Mikkola, Finding out what new employees know (conversation analysis of recorded orientation lectures), Työelämän tutkimus: https://journal.fi/tyoelamantutkimus/article/download/87105/46030/133414
inGame: the person's job record (employer, position, workplace) and the new-coworker event carry who and where; the speaker's habit is a line choice by trait; needs: a recorded orientation or training session

turns.summary: The trainer asks as if everyone already knows and moves on at the first right answer.
turns.writesBack: a newcomer who did not know goes quiet; a mood note of feeling behind

turns.summary: The trainer just tells the rule without asking anything.
turns.writesBack: nothing is learned about what the newcomer knows; no tie change

turns.summary: The newcomer says they have not done this before and the trainer slows down to show it.
turns.writesBack: a small friendly tie with the trainer; a journal note about the first week
